one_liner: Go server adding Kafka-style partitioned, replicated logs on top of NATS; self-reports ~1.1x NATS JetStream publish throughput on one node.
what_it_does: Liftbridge is a standalone server that attaches durable streams to NATS subjects. A partition leader sequences whatever is published to a subject into an append-only log, and consumers replay it from an offset, a timestamp or a cursor. On top of that it adds Kafka-like partitioning, ISR replication, consumer groups, retention, log compaction and reverse reads. The API is its own gRPC service, not JetStream's NATS-protocol API; official clients exist for Go, Java and Rust. It needs a NATS server, which can be external or embedded in the same process.
how_it_is_fast: Streams replicate with a Kafka-style in-sync-replica (ISR) protocol and use Raft (hashicorp/raft) only for cluster metadata, so each message goes into one log rather than a Raft log plus a message log. The partition leader drains its NATS subscription into batches of up to 1,024 messages (batch.max.messages). It appends each batch to a segmented commit log with a memory-mapped offset index, and segment writes go to the OS page cache with no fsync. The January 2026 release that added the benchmark also added an RF=1 fast path. For LEADER/NONE acks it skips the commit queue and advances the high watermark once per batch, and clients can pipeline publishes over the streaming gRPC PublishAsync call.
when_to_use: You already run NATS and want durable, replayable, partitioned streams on existing subjects without changing the publishers.
A Go shop that wants Kafka-like semantics (consumer groups, compaction, retention, offset/timestamp replay) from a single self-contained binary with embedded NATS instead of a JVM cluster.
Small-message ingest (the benchmark uses 256-byte messages) in the roughly 100-250K msgs/sec per-partition range, where the client can batch or pipeline publishes.
A single-region cluster run with RF=3, AckPolicy_ALL and min.insync.replicas=2 to get quorum-acknowledged, at-least-once delivery.
Edge or IoT nodes running RF=1, where losing leader-acked but unflushed messages on a crash is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: You need fsync-level durability. Segment writes are never fsynced and the high watermark is checkpointed only every 5 s by default. A configurable sync policy exists only as a proposal in the repo's own bottleneck analysis.

Multi-region clusters: an engineer who deployed it reported on HN that cross-region latency throttles the Raft metadata protocol, which slows stream creation and ISR changes. Federated clustering is only on the roadmap.

You need transactions, exactly-once or idempotent producers, message compression, tiered storage, Prometheus metrics or SASL auth. The roadmap lists all of these as not done, and no release has shipped since v26.01.1.
Read-heavy fan-out: the repo's own analysis flags one-message-at-a-time reads, one gRPC Send per message and per-message allocations on the subscribe path.
Choosing it over JetStream mainly for speed: the ~1.1x margin is against an unsourced JetStream figure, and no replicated or AckPolicy_ALL throughput is published.

integration.form: module (standalone Go server; prebuilt linux/darwin/windows tarballs, .deb/.rpm packages and a ghcr.io Docker image; clients speak gRPC)
integration.dependencies: NATS Server v2.10.0+ (external, or embedded in-process via nats.embedded); hashicorp/raft + raft-boltdb (metadata), gRPC, tysonmote/gommap (mmap index), google/tink (encryption at rest), casbin (authorization); clients: go-liftbridge v2 (official), plus Java and Rust official clients and community Node.js/Python clients
integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.25.6+ to build from source (raised from Go 1.21 in v26.01.1)
integration.platforms: Release binaries for linux, darwin and windows on amd64 and arm64; CI tests run only on ubuntu-latest
integration.thread_safety: The server accepts many concurrent publishers and subscribers, but a single segment write mutex serializes appends within a partition (per the repo's bottleneck analysis). On the client side, the repo's bench tool warns that pub-batch > 1 combined with more than one concurrent publisher 'may hang due to go-liftbridge client limitations'.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it shares NATS subjects, so plain NATS publishers can feed Liftbridge streams unchanged, but JetStream streams, consumers and client APIs do not carry over; reading and managing streams needs a Liftbridge gRPC client

gotchas: The headline configuration (4 concurrent publishers with pub-batch=100) is the same combination the repo's bench/producer tool prints a warning about possibly hanging because of go-liftbridge client limitations.

The default ack policy is LEADER, which acks after the leader's page-cache write. With RF=1 (the default replication factor) and no fsync, acked messages can be lost in a crash; uncommitted messages can also be lost during a leader change.

Two defaults to change: anonymous telemetry is on and sends instance ID, OS, CPU and memory info to telemetry.basekick.net every 24 h (turn it off with telemetry.enabled: false or LIFTBRIDGE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false), and partition data lives under /tmp/liftbridge/<namespace> unless you set data.dir.

Open security reports: #470, where Subscribe applies the consumer-group replacement (closing the legitimate subscriber) before checking authorization, with fix PR #471 still open; and #468, where NATS credentials embedded in server URLs are written verbatim to the startup log.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over NATS JetStream when you want Kafka-style partitioned logs with ISR replication, consumer groups and compaction layered onto an existing NATS deployment; if you want the default, better-supported choice inside nats-server, pick JetStream, since the throughput edge is marginal and unverified. Redpanda and Fluvio are catalogued as Kafka replacements with multi-level published numbers (Redpanda up to 1 GB/s). Choose those when throughput or tail latency at scale is the main requirement, and Liftbridge when you want a lighter, Go-native service tied to NATS.
verified_claims_summary: Using its own bench/producer tool, the repo reports ~241K msgs/sec (P99 2.0 ms) for 4 concurrent publishers, each pipelining 100 async publishes, on a single node with RF=1 and 256-byte messages. The message size comes from the CHANGELOG, and the ack policy is not stated, but the tool's default and the README example are both leader. The ~220K msgs/sec NATS JetStream figure is quoted as 'similar settings (pubbatch=100, file storage, RF=1)' with no source, version, hardware or harness, and no hardware, OS, Go version or run length is given for either side, so the ~1.1x is a cross-run comparison, not a side-by-side measurement.
status_note: Active in name: Basekick Labs revived it with v26.01.1 in January 2026 after no releases since v1.9.0 in September 2022. Commits since then are mostly dependabot bumps plus one Docker fix (last 2026-07-15), and the roadmap's v26.02 items have not shipped. It is Apache-2.0 with prebuilt binaries and packages, so it is usable as-is.
